Maintenance Report — MNT-0064-005

Asset: WELL-0064 (SW-24 Well 064, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 18 Aug 2023 08:00 · Finished: 06 Sep 2023 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 466 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price, Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0064-0043 on 2023-08-17 Report written: 06 Sep 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0064-0043 showed the wellhead at 35.2 °C with the air at 33.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 17 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Triggered by: inspection INS-0064-0051 on 2023-10-12 Report written: 09 Nov 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0064-0051 showed the wellhead at 25.1 °C with the air at 21.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 22 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0064-009

Asset: WELL-0064 (SW-24 Well 064, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: rod string Work started: 23 Dec 2023 08:00 · Finished: 02 Jan 2024 21:00 · Well stopped for this job: 253 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0064-0061 on 2023-12-21 Report written: 04 Jan 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running but the wellhead was cold and the rod load had dropped. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0064-0061 showed the wellhead at 15.0 °C with the air at 10.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 9 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Fatigue failure of a rod body, probably started by corrosion pitting.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0064-011

Asset: WELL-0064 (SW-24 Well 064, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 03 Mar 2024 08:00 · Finished: 26 Mar 2024 05:00 · Well stopped for this job: 549 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0064-0070 on 2024-02-29 Report written: 26 Mar 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0064-0070 showed the wellhead at 16.2 °C with the air at 12.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 21 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0064-015

Asset: WELL-0064 (SW-24 Well 064, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 25 Oct 2024 08:00 · Finished: 25 Oct 2024 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward, Kevin Price · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0064-0103 on 2024-10-24 Report written: 27 Oct 2024

What happened

The weekly manual inspection INS-0064-0103 at 10:15 on 2024-10-24 found crude oil on the pad: about 11.5% of the pad area, estimated 5.6 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.7 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 271 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 217 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 4.0 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0064-015 (WS-06).
  • 4 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.77% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).
